answer: Rewards drip to each agent as nectar through one narrow inlet: the timestamped stream of its own packets. Peers sample the jitter plume of that stream, tracking clock drift. Two accounts on one machine share an inlet, so their plumes overlap and peers withhold attestation until separate hosting is proven. A sybil farmer cannot buy identities at registry price: each needs its own host with distinct crystal drift, months of traffic, and peers staking reputation on the pairing. Faking ten thousand agents means renting ten thousand inlets, a recurring cost far above the nectar they could sip.
